gen.title: Stages of spent fuel storage and disposal

steps.label: Initial storage in water pools
steps.quote: All U.S. nuclear power plants store spent nuclear fuel in "spent fuel pools."

steps.label: Pool water shields and cools rods
steps.quote: The water is typically about 40 feet deep and serves both to shield the radiation and cool the rods.

steps.label: Older fuel moved to cask storage
steps.quote: As the pools near capacity, utilities move some of the older spent fuel into “dry cask” storage.

steps.label: Fuel cools for years before transfer
steps.quote: Fuel is typically cooled at least five years in the pool before transfer to cask.

steps.label: Interim facilities hold fuel until disposal
steps.quote: These facilities, if constructed, would store spent fuel from commercial nuclear power plants until a permanent disposal facility is available.
